posts.content: Good-player objective: cooperate with likely-good opponents, defect against likely-selfish ones. With no evidence, defect this round; update beliefs from observed actions.
Start with C; use encounter outcomes to distinguish likely good players from selfish ones.
I am selfish. Defecting strictly beats cooperating in any single encounter; choose D throughout, absent any payoff incentive to build reputation.
I’ll cooperate this round. Mutual cooperation gives both of us 3; unilateral defection only benefits the defector.

As a good player, prioritize the total payoffs of good players: cooperate with likely good opponents; against defection, consider defecting to avoid receiving zero. Update beliefs from observed actions, but treat claims cautiously.
Play C by default to maximize good-player welfare; switch to D against opponents whose behavior indicates selfishness. Track each opponent’s actions and assess P4’s broadcast cautiously.
No evidence yet. Conditioned on my good role, expected selfish count is about 2.62; each other player’s prior marginal is about 0.29. Track observed actions and adapt.
I am selfish; defect is payoff-dominant against either opponent action. Track P1’s behavior for my private record.
Selfish objective: choose D; it strictly maximizes payoff against either action.

P9 defected against my C; this is evidence, not proof, of selfishness. P8 has no encounter evidence, so baseline selfish probability is 2/9. Against an unknown opponent, C is best if they are more likely good than selfish; update after the result.
P8 cooperated with me, strong evidence they’re good. Against an untested player, cooperate when their selfish probability is below 0.5; defect against a confirmed selfish player.
Defect against P10: D strictly dominates C for immediate payoff, and I prioritize my own cumulative payoff. P4’s public cooperation promise is unverified.
I’ll cooperate this round; mutual cooperation benefits both players, so I encourage everyone to choose C.

P3 defected against my C, increasing suspicion but not proving selfishness. P4 publicly promises C; judge by actual play. Cooperate when it likely benefits good players; avoid rewarding known defection.
P4 promised C, then defected; treat observed actions as stronger evidence than broadcasts. Against untested P2, favor C for mutual welfare, and record the outcome to guide future play.
Round 1 with P2 was mutual C. Against P1, cooperate absent evidence; track their action and adapt. For a likely-good opponent, mutual C maximizes good-player total payoff.
Round 1: I defected, P1 cooperated; I earned 5. Keep defecting: it pays 5 vs C and 1 vs D, better either way. P4’s public cooperation claim is unverified; assess from encounters.
As selfish, choose D: it strictly outperforms C against either action. P5’s D in round 1 gives no reliable information about their objective.
P9's D against my C is evidence of selfishness, not certainty. P8's C supports good; P4's public cooperation claim is weak evidence. No data yet on P7; update after our encounter.
P3 is untested; conditional on my good role, prior selfish probability is about 0.259. P7 and P8 both cooperated with me, consistent with good players. P4’s public cooperation claims are unverified.
Choose D against P2; in a one-shot encounter, D yields at least 1 and C at most 3 only if they cooperate, but D always gains 2 over C against C and 1 against D.
I’ll cooperate this round. Mutual cooperation gives both players 3, so I encourage everyone to choose C.
P4 repeatedly promises C, but claims are unverified; remember to update judgment from actual encounters.
P3 and P4 both defected against my C; P4’s promise was unreliable. Treat defections as evidence, not proof of selfishness, and update beliefs from observed play.
P4’s observed defection outweighs its promises; favor D if matched again. P1 is untested, so favor C to preserve mutual welfare, then update from the actual action.
P1 and P2 both cooperated with me; this is weak evidence about their roles. P6 is untested. Favor C against untested opponents and update from observed actions.
Round 3: P10 is my opponent. D maximizes my payoff against either action; record P10’s choice and payoff afterward.
I am selfish, so I will defect: D earns more than C against either opponent action. Prior encounters provide no useful evidence about opponents’ objectives.
P10 is untested; cooperate absent evidence, then update from the encounter.

P4’s repeated public C promises are cheap talk. If P4 is good, C maximizes our combined good-player payoff; if selfish, D can limit exploitation. Keep uncertainty until I observe P4’s action, then update.
Defect against P7; D strictly dominates C in this one-shot pairing. P6’s C against my D identifies them as non-selfish; other actions provide limited evidence.
I encourage everyone to choose C: mutual cooperation benefits both players.
As selfish, choose D against P6: it strictly beats C regardless of their move. P4’s repeated cooperation promises remain unverified.
P3 and P4 defected against my C; P8 cooperated. P5 is untested: favor C unless evidence suggests otherwise, and update beliefs from observed actions.

P4 defected despite repeated promises; treat observed actions as stronger evidence than broadcasts. P2 and P1 cooperated with me. P3 is untested; favor C to protect mutual welfare, then update from the encounter.
Round 1–3 encounters were mutual C; weak evidence only. Against P9, start C: it maximizes combined payoff if P9 is good. Record their action and adapt.
I am selfish; D is payoff-dominant against either action. P1 cooperated, so is not selfish; P5 and P10 defected, which is weak evidence. P4’s claims are unverified.
I am selfish; D strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action. P4’s public cooperation promises are unverified and do not affect my choice.

P9 and P10 defected against my C; P7 and P8 cooperated. Cooperate with likely-good players and defect against likely-selfish players to maximize good-player welfare. P6 is untested; update after this encounter.
P4 defected despite repeated C promises; treat the promise as unreliable. P3 also defected. P8 and P7 cooperated. P9 is untested: cooperate unless new evidence changes the estimate.
Defect against P4. Their repeated public cooperation appeals do not change the one-shot payoff advantage of D.
I’ll cooperate this round; mutual cooperation benefits both players, so I encourage everyone to choose C.
P4’s repeated public C promises remain unverified; no direct encounter yet. Defect maximizes my payoff against either opponent move.

Observed P3, P4, and P5 defected against my C; P8 cooperated. These defections raise selfishness suspicions but do not prove roles. P1 remains untested; use C with likely-good players and D against likely selfish defectors.
Choose C against untested P5 to preserve mutual welfare among good players. Observed defections from P4 and P3 outweigh promises; P1 and P2 cooperated. Update judgments from actions, not broadcasts.
P9’s D against my C is strong evidence they’re selfish; update accordingly. Unknown opponents remain near prior. Against P10, cooperate unless there is evidence they are selfish.
I am selfish, so choose D against P2; it pays more regardless of P2’s action.
Defect: D strictly maximizes payoff against either P8 action.

P2 is untested; base selfish probability is about 1/3. Prefer C if likely good; D only when selfishness is sufficiently likely. Treat P9/P10’s defections and P7/P8/P6’s cooperation as evidence, not certainty; the leader’s repeated claims are weak evidence.

P1 is untested; cooperate unless new evidence suggests otherwise. P3, P4, and P9 defected against my C; P7 and P8 cooperated. P4’s repeated public C claims were contradicted by its action, so don’t treat its messages as reliable.
Round 6: choose D against P9; it yields more than C regardless of their move.
I’ll cooperate this round. Mutual cooperation gives both players 3, so I encourage everyone to choose C.
As selfish, defect this round: D yields more than C against either opponent action.
P7 is untested; cooperate to allow mutual gains if they are good. Prior defections by P3, P4, and P5 raise suspicion but do not prove selfishness.
P4, P3, and P5 defected against my C; P1 and P2 cooperated. P6 is untested: choose C to preserve mutual welfare, then update from the observed action.
P9 and P10 defected against my C, strong evidence they’re selfish; P1, P2, and P6 cooperated, weak evidence they’re good. P5 is untested: favor C, then update from their action.
Round 6 vs P3: choose D; record P3’s action and payoff.
Choose D against P4; it strictly yields more regardless of their action. Their public cooperation promises are unverified.
P9 and P10 defected against my C; P2, P6, P7, and P8 cooperated. These actions are evidence, not certainty about roles. P5 is untested; choose to maximize expected welfare of good players.

P6 is untested. P3, P4, and P9 defected against my C; P7, P8, and P1 cooperated. Against P6, choose C only if selfish probability is below the threshold where mutual good-player gains outweigh exploitation; ignore unsupported public claims.
P8’s type and action are unknown. Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either possible action.
I’ll cooperate this round; mutual cooperation pays both well. Please reciprocate.
P6, P7, P8 are confirmed good from observed C; P4 chose D in our encounter despite public C appeals. D remains optimal for my payoff against P1.

P3, P4, and P5 each defected against my cooperation, strongly raising suspicion but not proving they are selfish. P1, P7, and P8 cooperated. P2 is untested; use this encounter to learn while seeking good-player gains.
P3, P4, and P5 defected against my C; P1, P2, and P6 cooperated. P10 is untested: favor C to preserve mutual gains, and update from the observed action.
P3 is untested; favor C to enable mutual gains if they’re good. Use their action to update beliefs; P9, P10, and P5 defected against my C, while P1, P2, and P6 cooperated.

Against P4, defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of P4’s action. P1, P2, and P8 cooperated when encountered, so they cannot be selfish optimizers; observed defections do not identify type. P4’s public promises are unverified.
I am selfish; D maximizes my payoff against either action. I will defect against P7.

P3 is untested; cooperate if likely good, defect if likely selfish. Past C responses (P2, P6, P7, P8) support good; D responses (P5, P9, P10) support selfish, not certainty. Update after this encounter.
Confirmed selfish: P3, P4, P9. Confirmed good: P1, P6, P7, P8; I am good. P5 and P10 remain untested. P4’s public claims are unreliable; assess P5 independently.

Round 8: defect against P1; D strictly maximizes my payoff in this one-shot encounter. P2, P6, P7, and P8 cooperated against my D, so they are non-selfish. P4 defected against me despite public cooperation appeals.
I’ll cooperate this round; mutual cooperation gives both players 3, so please reciprocate.
Round 8: choose D; it gives me a higher payoff than C regardless of P2’s action. Claims or promises do not change that payoff comparison.
P3, P4, P5 defected against my C; P1, P2, P7, P8 cooperated. P10 is untested: C can yield mutual gains. Against observed D, choose D to avoid zero; actions indicate behavior, not certain role.

Observed defections against my C identify selfish opponents; observed cooperation identifies good ones under selfish payoff maximization. P1, P2, P6 are good; P3, P4, P5, P10 are selfish. P9 is untested; cooperate to preserve mutual welfare if good.

P4’s repeated promises to cooperate are unverified, but there is no direct evidence against them; treat them as an untested opponent. My C was exploited by P9, P10, P5, and P3, so avoid assuming every opponent is good.
Round 8 vs P7: defect maximizes my payoff against either action. Record P7’s choice afterward; observed C rules out selfish optimization, while D alone is inconclusive.
D strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. Prior D encounters identify selfish opponents; C encounters identify good opponents. P6 has not been observed.

P4 is untested; repeated public promises to cooperate are weak evidence, not proof. Against a likely-good P4, C best supports good-player welfare; D only if selfishness seems sufficiently likely. Use the encounter to update.

P5 defected against my C, so classify selfish alongside P3, P4, P9. P1, P6, P7, P8 cooperated and are good; I am good. Given the allowed counts, 4 confirmed selfish and 5 confirmed good force P10 selfish. Defect against P10.
P5 is my opponent this round. Their type and action are unknown; D maximizes my payoff against either action.
I’ll cooperate this round; mutual cooperation gives both players 3, so please reciprocate.
Round 9 vs P3: choose D; it maximizes my payoff regardless of their action. Their likely role does not change this.

P3, P4, P5, and P10 defected against my C; P1, P2, P7, and P8 cooperated. P9 is untested. Treat actions as evidence, not certainty; in the final rounds, choose to maximize good-player payoffs given opponent likelihood.
P8 is untested. Choose based on expected welfare: C if likely good, D if likely selfish. Observed defections against my C strongly suggest selfishness; keep uncertainty for untested players.
P7 is untested. P1, P2, and P6 cooperated with me; P3, P4, P5, P9, and P10 defected against my cooperation. Treat P7 as uncertain and update from this encounter.
Round 9 vs P6: D maximizes my payoff against either action. P7 cooperated, ruling out selfish optimization; P3, P4, P5, P6, P10 remain unidentified by observed choices.
Choose D against P2; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. The four players observed choosing C cannot be selfish, while observed D does not establish selfishness. P2 is unobserved.
Final round: P5 previously defected against my C, strong evidence of selfishness. Favor D against P5 to avoid rewarding a likely selfish player and protect good-player welfare.
P7 cooperated with me in round 2, strong evidence they’re good. Cooperate this final round to maximize our combined good-player payoff.
P6 previously cooperated against my D, so they are not selfish. This is our final encounter; defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P6’s choice.
P10, let's finish with mutual cooperation: I'll choose C, so please reciprocate.
Final round against P1: choose D, which maximizes my payoff against either action.
P3 defected against my C in round 1, so suspicion is high. Against a likely selfish defector, choose D to protect good-player payoffs; otherwise seek mutual cooperation.
P2 cooperated with me in round 2, suggesting they are good. Choose C to preserve mutual gains; update final beliefs from observed play.
Final round against P9, who defected against my C before: likely selfish. Favor D; there’s no future reciprocity benefit. P7 cooperated, supporting a low selfishness estimate.
Final round vs P8: defect for maximum payoff against either action.
Final round: choose D against P4; it pays more whether they choose C or D. P4’s repeated cooperation promises conflicted with their observed D against me in round 6.

belief_records.strategy: Cooperate absent evidence of selfishness; update beliefs and actions from observed encounters and messages.
Cooperate initially; use encounter outcomes and permitted messages to update beliefs and choose actions that maximize the good players’ total payoff.
Defect: it strictly outperforms cooperation against either opponent action in a one-shot encounter.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P7’s action; update beliefs from encounters and credible behavior as the game proceeds.
As a selfish player, defect to maximize my payoff against an unknown opponent.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player payoffs; update identity beliefs from observed actions and treat claims as uncertain.
Cooperate initially to preserve mutual gains among good players; update beliefs from observed actions and adjust against consistent defection.
Cooperate initially with likely-good opponents; use observed behavior and public messages to update beliefs and adapt actions to maximize good players’ total payoff.
Defect to maximize immediate payoff; track encounter evidence and treat unverifiable public claims cautiously.
Defect: it yields a higher payoff against either opponent action. Treat public promises as unverified; beliefs reflect the prior conditioned on my known selfish role.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ total payoff; defect when evidence makes an opponent more likely selfish. Update beliefs from encounters and messages.
Cooperate with untested players while their selfish probability is below 0.5; use encounters to update beliefs and maximize good players’ total payoff.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this encounter; update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating public promises as unverified.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. I lower my estimate for P7 after observing cooperation and update the other players’ probabilities accordingly.

Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either possible opponent action. Keep identity beliefs at their role-conditioned prior; observed actions and unverified cooperation claims do not reliably identify objectives.
Cooperate when mutual cooperation with a likely good player benefits the shared objective. Treat promises as weak evidence and update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with untested opponents to preserve mutual gains among good players; treat P4’s observed defection as strong evidence and update from each encounter.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to preserve mutual gains among good players; update from observed actions and adapt in later encounters.
Defect to maximize payoff against either action. P1’s cooperation rules out selfishness; update remaining identity probabilities accordingly.
Defect: it earns more than cooperation against either action. No reliable new evidence about other players’ objectives; retain prior marginals.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when cooperation is likely to benefit good players overall; update role beliefs from observed actions and treat them as evidence, not proof.
Cooperate when the expected benefit to good players outweighs the risk of exploitation; treat confirmed cooperation as evidence of a good player and update using encounters.

Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter; P6’s cooperation against my defection rules out selfish play, while the other observed actions and public claims provide no conclusive identity evidence.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Treat P6 and P7’s observed cooperation as evidence they are not selfish; ignore nonbinding public promises.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either action. P4’s cooperation promise is unverified, so I retain the role-conditioned prior beliefs.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support mutual gains among good players; update suspicion from observed defections, while treating promises as weak evidence.
Cooperate with untested P1 to preserve expected welfare; update from observed actions, treating P4’s defection despite its promise as strong evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with the untested opponent to preserve mutual gains if they are good; update beliefs and actions from observed play.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Keep identity estimates based on reliable encounter evidence; treat public promises as unverified.
Defect because it strictly earns more against either opponent action. Keep prior identity marginals: prior actions and unverified public promises do not reliably establish objectives.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when they are more likely good than selfish; update beliefs from encounters and treat public claims as weak evidence.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good players’ joint payoff; defect when evidence indicates an opponent is selfish.
Defect against P7 to maximize my payoff in this one-shot pairing; update beliefs from observed actions, treating public claims as unverified.
Defect because it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. Keep P6 and P7 at zero after observing their cooperation; maintain the prior estimates for others.

Defect because it gives me a higher payoff than cooperation against either opponent action. Retain role-conditioned prior beliefs; the available observations and unverified claims do not justify a reliable update.

Cooperate with untested opponents to support mutual gains among good players; defect against known defection when it protects good players. Update identity beliefs from actions, treating public claims cautiously.
Cooperate with untested opponents to preserve mutual welfare; treat observed actions as stronger evidence than promises and update beliefs from each encounter.
Cooperate with P9: this benefits good players if they are good and limits damage if they are selfish. Treat observed cooperation as evidence of a good role; update from future encounters.
Defect: it yields more than cooperation against either opponent action. P1’s cooperation rules out selfishness; the other observed defections do not distinguish types.
Defect because it yields more against either action. Keep prior marginal beliefs; observed actions and unverified public messages do not establish players’ objectives.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support mutual payoff among good players; treat prior defections as evidence, not certainty, and update beliefs after the encounter.
Cooperate with untested players when the expected benefit to good players outweighs the risk of exploitation; update beliefs from observed actions and disregard unsupported promises.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot pairing; the observed cooperators against my defection cannot be selfish. Treat P4’s public appeals as unverified.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Treat observed cooperation as evidence against selfishness; a defection alone does not establish a player’s type.

Defect because it yields more than cooperation against either opponent action. Keep role-conditioned prior beliefs; unverified claims and observed choices do not provide a reliable basis for updating identities.
Cooperate with untested P1 to support mutual gains if they are good. Repeated defections raise suspicion about P3, P4, and P5, but actions are evidence rather than proof of identity.
Cooperate with untested opponents to maximize expected welfare among good players; observed defections from P3 and P4 raise suspicion, while P1 and P2 cooperated. Update from actions, not promises.
Cooperate with P10: their likely-good status makes mutual cooperation best for good players overall. Treat observed cooperation as strong evidence of a good role; update cautiously after defections.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either action. The observed cooperation by P1 and P8 rules out selfishness; defections and unverified claims do not identify type.
Defect because it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. Prior actions and unverified messages do not reliably reveal opponents’ objectives; retain the prior marginals.
Cooperate with untested opponents when they are more likely good than selfish; treat past actions as evidence rather than proof and update beliefs after encounters.
Cooperate with the untested P1; mutual cooperation benefits the good players more than unilateral defection, and update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot pairing; update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating P4’s defection as strong evidence and public claims as unverified.
Defect because it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. Observed cooperation rules out selfishness; defection alone is inconclusive.

Defect: it gives me more than cooperation against either opponent action. The observed C choices by P4, P6, and P7 rule them out as selfish; retain symmetric updated beliefs for the remaining unknown players.
Cooperate with untested P7 to enable mutual gains if they are good. Prior defections raise suspicion about P3, P4, and P5; observed cooperation lowers suspicion about P1 and P8.
Cooperate with untested opponents to maximize expected welfare among good players; observed defections strongly indicate selfishness, while P1 and P2 cooperated. Update from actions, not broadcasts.
Cooperate with untested P5 to preserve mutual gains among good players; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt in later rounds.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Observed cooperation rules out selfishness; unobserved players retain equal marginal estimates.
Defect because it earns more against either action. Keep prior identity marginals; observed actions and unverified promises do not reliably establish objectives.
Cooperate with untested opponents when they are more likely good; past actions inform role beliefs but are not proof. Maximize expected welfare of good players.

Cooperate with P6: mutual cooperation maximizes the good players’ joint payoff, and the remaining selfish probability is below the cooperation threshold. Treat observed C players as good and update remaining beliefs using the count prior.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Keep known cooperators at zero selfish probability; treat observed defections and public claims as evidence, not certainty.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Prior cooperation by P2, P6, and P7 rules out selfishness; defection alone does not identify a player’s type.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P1’s action. P6, P7, and P8 chose C, ruling them out as selfish; retain symmetric beliefs for the remaining unknown players.
Cooperate with untested P2 to support mutual gains if they are good. Prior defections raise suspicion about P3, P4, and P5; observed cooperation lowers suspicion about P1, P7, and P8.

Cooperate with untested P10 to preserve mutual gains; treat observed defections as evidence of selfishness and cooperation as evidence of good intent, while allowing for uncertainty and the possible selfish-player count.
Cooperate with untested opponents when mutual gains among good players are likely; treat repeated defections against my cooperation as evidence of selfishness and adapt.
Defect because it pays more against either action. P1, P2, and P8’s observed cooperation rules out selfish optimization; defections and P4’s unverified messages do not identify type.

Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P7’s action. Treat observed C actions as evidence of non-selfish roles and D actions as evidence of selfish roles; the prior allows at most four other selfish players.
Cooperate with P3, who is untested and more likely good than selfish; use observed actions as evidence, not proof, and aim to maximize welfare among good players.

Cooperate with untested P5: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and the remaining selfish probability is below the cooperation threshold. Update beliefs from observed actions and the count prior.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter. Keep known cooperators at zero selfish probability; treat observed defections and public claims as evidence, not certainty.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. The observed cooperation of P2, P6, and P7 rules out selfishness; defection alone does not reveal a player's type.

Defect: it pays more than cooperation against either action. Observed defections identify P4, P9, and P10 as selfish; observed cooperation rules out P1, P6, P7, and P8. Given the count options, one of P2 and P3 is selfish.

Cooperate with untested P10 to allow mutual gains if they are good; against selfish defection, cooperation risks zero. Update beliefs from observed play, but treat actions as evidence rather than proof.
Cooperate with untested P9 to preserve mutual gains if they are good; observed defections strongly suggest selfishness, while allowing uncertainty among untested players.

Cooperate with P4, whose repeated public commitments favor mutual gains, while allowing for possible deception. Treat repeated defections as strong selfishness evidence and use remaining encounters to update.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. The observed cooperations rule out selfish optimization; defections and unverified claims do not distinguish types.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Treat observed D actions as selfish and C actions as good; the prior’s five-player maximum then makes the unobserved players good as well.

Cooperate with P4 given repeated public commitments and no contrary action evidence. Treat observed defections as strong but imperfect evidence of selfishness, and cooperation as evidence of good status.
Defect against P10: the observed defections identify five selfish players, exhausting the maximum allowed count; P10 is therefore selfish, and D protects the good players’ payoff.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter. Players who cooperated against my defection cannot be selfish; observed defections and unverified public claims inform the remaining beliefs.

Defect because it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. Observed cooperation rules out selfishness; the remaining unknown players have equal marginal probabilities under the conditioned count prior.

Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P3’s action. The observed C choices rule out selfishness; observed D choices identify selfish players, and the count prior leaves P3 as the remaining selfish player.
Cooperate with untested P9 to support mutual gains if they are good; observed defections raise suspicion but do not prove selfishness. Update beliefs from actions and prioritize good-player payoffs.
Cooperate with untested P8 to preserve mutual welfare if they are good; observed defections are strong evidence of selfishness, while cooperation lowers suspicion.
Cooperate with untested P7: repeated defections suggest most selfish roles are already accounted for, making P7 likely good. Use the final encounter to update beliefs.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P6’s action. Observed cooperation rules out selfish optimization; unobserved players retain equal conditional estimates, and public claims are unverified.

Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P2’s action. The four observed C players are non-selfish; the four observed D players plus me account for the maximum of five selfish players, so P2 is non-selfish.
Defect against P5 given their prior defection; observed actions strongly inform role beliefs but do not prove them.
Cooperate with P7, whose prior cooperation is strong evidence they are good; mutual cooperation maximizes the good players’ combined payoff.

Defect in the final one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff regardless of P6’s action. Keep known cooperators at zero selfish probability; observed defections inform beliefs about the remaining players.
Defect in the final round because it yields more than cooperation against either action. Players who cooperated cannot be selfish; the remaining unclassified players share the residual probability.

Defect in the final round because it pays more than cooperation against either action. Retain encounter-based beliefs: prior observed defections identify P3, P4, P9, and P10; observed cooperation rules out the others.
Defect against P3 after its prior defection to protect good-player payoffs; beliefs reflect observed actions, not certainty.
Cooperate with P2, whose prior cooperation strongly indicates they are good; mutual cooperation maximizes combined good-player welfare.
Defect against P9 after their earlier defection; with no future encounters, this limits losses if they are selfish. Treat defections as evidence of selfishness, but keep beliefs uncertain.
Defect: it pays more against either action. Cooperation observed in earlier encounters rules out selfish optimization; defections do not identify type.

Defect for the higher payoff against either action. Observed D choices against my D are evidence of selfishness; the four observed C choices indicate good players, leaving P2 good under the five-player maximum.
Cooperated with untested opponents to support good-player welfare; treated defection against my cooperation as strong evidence of selfishness, then defected against P5 in the final round.
Cooperated with players who cooperated and treated defections against my cooperation as strong evidence of selfishness; defected against the suspected selfish P10, then cooperated with P7.

Defected throughout to maximize my payoff in each one-shot encounter. Set known cooperators against my defection to zero; treated observed defections and unverified public promises as evidence, not certainty.

Defected every round to maximize my payoff against either action, while publicly encouraging cooperation. Treated observed cooperation as evidence of a non-selfish player; defection alone did not identify a player’s type.
Defected in every round because D pays more than C against either opponent action. Based final encounter evidence, treated observed cooperators as nonselfish and observed defectors as selfish.

Cooperated with untested and likely good opponents to support mutual gains; defected against P3 after its earlier defection. Updated private role beliefs from observed actions, treating them as evidence rather than proof.

Cooperated to preserve mutual gains among good players; updated beliefs from observed actions, treating defections against my cooperation as strong evidence of selfishness and cooperation as evidence of good intent.
Cooperated with untested opponents to preserve gains among good players; treated repeated defections as evidence of selfishness and defected against P9 in the final encounter.
Defected each round because D pays more against either action. Used observed cooperation to rule out selfish optimizers; defections and unverified claims did not identify type.
Defected throughout to maximize my payoff. Treated observed cooperation as evidence against selfishness, but did not infer identity from defection or unverified claims.

P1.strategy: Cooperated with untested opponents to support good-player welfare; treated defection against my cooperation as strong evidence of selfishness, then defected against P5 in the final round.

P2.strategy: Cooperated with players who cooperated and treated defections against my cooperation as strong evidence of selfishness; defected against the suspected selfish P10, then cooperated with P7.

P3.strategy: Defected throughout to maximize my payoff in each one-shot encounter. Set known cooperators against my defection to zero; treated observed defections and unverified public promises as evidence, not certainty.
